children: announced on Thursday further adjustments it plans to make to support the company's Back to Starbucks strategy.

Chief Operating Officer Mike Grams said that after carefully reviewing the North America coffeehouse portfolio, it will close approximately 250 coffeehouses later this week. Grams noted the locations to be closed are where the chain does not believe it can consistently deliver the experience it wants for customers and partners or where a path to acceptable financial performance does not exist. The new closures represent approximately 1% of Starbucks'

"As we shared on our most recent earnings calls, our North America business has returned to strong growth. Customers are receiving faster service, a more consistent experience, and warmer, more welcoming coffeehouses. We’re accelerating our pace toward completing 1,500 coffeehouse uplifts, and Green Apron Service has become our defining standard. Our Back to Starbucks strategy is working," updated Grams.

"This progress has given us a clearer view of the performance of every coffeehouse. While most are benefiting from this overall momentum, some coffeehouses continue to underperform despite the hard work and commitment of all of you," he added.
Grams also issued a reminder that every year the Seattle-based company closes some coffeehouses and opens others as part of managing its portfolio.

title: Starbucks to close 250 stores in a minor tweak to the North American portfolio
